title: UPI AutoPay vs eNACH: Differences, Limits and Mandate Setup
summary: Compare UPI AutoPay vs eNACH on debit limits, mandate setup, authentication, bank coverage and use cases to choose recurring payment methods in India.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


If you operate a business collecting subscriptions, EMIs, premium payments or SIPs from customers, you will want a method for automatically deducting funds from the customer’s bank account. There are two widely used methods available in India for this type of process; UPI AutoPay and eNACH. Both methods allow businesses to obtain recurring payments from a customer’s bank account. However, they have different restrictions, speeds for setting up mandates, and types of recurring payments that may be suitable for each.


This article compares UPI AutoPay versus eNACH to help a business owner select the most appropriate option, or utilise both. The important distinction is between a recurring debit that can run without fresh authentication and the maximum amount your payment provider supports.


### Key Takeaways


- UPI AutoPay uses a customer’s UPI app for mandate approval; eNACH uses a supported bank-authentication flow.
- RBI’s AFA-free threshold for subsequent UPI recurring debits is ₹15,000 in most categories and ₹1 lakh for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit card bills.
- Our eNACH offering supports up to ₹1 crore per transaction, subject to bank, account and mandate limits. This is separate from the UPI AFA thresholds.
- Choose by payment amount, bank coverage, activation time and customer experience. Registration speed is different from debit and settlement timing.


##


What Is UPI AutoPay?


[UPI AutoPay](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-autopay/) allows a customer to establish a recurring payment mandate via the customer’s UPI App. After establishing a mandate via their UPI App, the customer will approve the mandate by utilizing their UPI PIN. Once approved by the customer, the business will then be able to debit the customer’s account according to the established schedule.


Establishment of mandates via UPI AutoPay is rapid. With our supported flow, mandate setup can take approximately 10 seconds, while authorisations and debits are processed in real time. Customer approval, app availability and bank responses can affect completion; setup speed is not a guaranteed settlement time.


The schedules supported by UPI AutoPay include daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly and annual cycles, along with other[customised cycle requirements](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/introduction) . These types of schedules make UPI AutoPay ideal for subscription services, OTT platforms, SaaS products, and consumer applications. Confirm the frequencies supported for your integration and payment mode.


##


What Is eNACH?


[eNACH](https://www.cashfree.com/enach/) represents the digital form of a traditional NACH (National Automated Clearing House) mandate. Businesses may debit a customer’s bank account on a scheduled basis once a customer has authorized the establishment of a digital mandate via their net banking service or debit card, with Aadhaar-based authentication available for supported banks and flows.


When an eNACH mandate is established using a debit card, it merely confirms who the customer is. Even if the debit card expires during the term of the mandate established under an eNACH mandate, the mandate remains valid.


Through our eNACH offering, mandate creation can take around 24 hours and mandates are typically active within one to two days, subject to bank processing. eNACH is suited for high-value EMIs, insurance premiums, SIPs and utility bill collections.


##


UPI AutoPay vs eNACH: Key Differences at a Glance


**Point of Comparison** **UPI AutoPay** **eNACH**


Where the mandate is set up In the customer’s UPI app, approved with UPI PIN Through the customer’s bank, using a supported net banking, debit card or Aadhaar flow


Indicative activation time with Cashfree About 10 seconds in a supported flow; subject to approval and bank response Typically 1 to 2 days; subject to bank processing


Subsequent debit amount ₹15,000 without fresh AFA in most categories; up to ₹1 lakh without fresh AFA for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit card bills, subject to product enablement Up to ₹1 crore per transaction in our eNACH offering, subject to bank, account and mandate limits


Best suited for Subscriptions, OTT, SaaS and consumer apps High-value EMIs, insurance, SIPs and utility bills


Who can use it Customers with a supported UPI-enabled account and app Customers whose bank, account type and authentication method support eNACH


For UPI AutoPay, registration and the first transaction require AFA; the two checks can be combined when processed together. The AFA-free thresholds apply to subsequent recurring debits. Check the[supported payment methods and account configuration](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/payment-modes) before enabling higher-value charges.


##


Difference Between UPI AutoPay and eNACH: Debit Limits and AFA


The main differences in UPI AutoPay and eNACH lie within the limits of recurring transactions. Under the[RBI’s Digital Payments E-mandate Framework, 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=13374) , subsequent recurring transactions may be processed without an additional factor of authentication (AFA) for up to ₹15,000 per transaction. For insurance premium transactions, mutual fund subscriptions and credit card bill payments, the limit of AFA-free transactions is ₹1 lakh per transaction. Any recurring transactions above these thresholds require AFA, where supported by the provider and payment mode.


These limits apply to the digital payment methods under RBI’s E-mandate Framework, including cards, UPI and Prepaid Payment Instruments. They are not the debit ceiling for eNACH, which runs on the NACH bank-debit system.


Our eNACH has a separate per-transaction ceiling from the RBI e-mandate AFA limits. Our eNACH supports debits up to ₹1 crore per transaction, subject to bank and mandate limits. Due to its larger transaction limitation, eNACH is suitable for businesses that process high-value debits such as large loan EMIs or B2B collections. For B2B collections, confirm account eligibility: our current eNACH flow supports eligible individual accounts with a single signatory; corporate accounts with multiple signatories require physical NACH.


##


UPI Mandate vs eNACH Mandate: Creation and Activation


UPI mandates are activated/created directly within the UPI application utilized by your customers. After entering the required UPI PIN information, the mandate will be active and your business will have permission to debit your customer at scheduled times. Treat the mandate as ready for collection only after the payment provider confirms its active status.


With eNACH, mandates are sent to your customers’ banks where their accounts will be authenticated through net banking, their debit card or another supported authentication flow. This typically takes 1-2 working days. In addition, physical NACH mandates often require several working days for approval.


Another key difference exists in the activation process. To use eNACH directly, a business typically needs a corporate user ID or sponsor-bank arrangement; most businesses access this through a payment provider.


Changes to a mandate also vary. When utilising our eNACH flow, changes to the authorised mandate amount or frequency may require a revised mandate and customer authorisation. For a variable or on-demand mandate, a debit within the already authorised maximum is different from changing that mandate. Confirm the supported update flow for your integration.


##


UPI AutoPay vs NACH: Paper Mandates, UMRN and Fees


Physical NACH mandates require signing of a paper form. Processing includes bank verification, so approval can take longer than a digital flow. eNACH replaces that process by using online authentication. Therefore, a UPI AutoPay vs NACH comparison should distinguish physical NACH from eNACH.


A unique reference number will be assigned to each NACH mandate. This is the Unique Mandate Reference Number (UMRN).


There may also be costs associated with NACH mandates depending upon the financial institution and service provider. Some possible costs include a one time cost of registering for the first use of a mandate, a fee for every transaction processed through a mandate, a fee if a debit transaction does not succeed, and a fee if you need to cancel or modify your mandate. Ask for the merchant pricing applicable to your agreement, including taxes and return charges. The RBI framework for cards,[PPI](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/ppi-interoperability/) and UPI prohibits charging customers for the e-mandate facility. Merchant processing fees and NACH bank charges are separate considerations.


##


How to Set Up Recurring Payment Methods in India


### UPI AutoPay Mandate Setup


1. At checkout, the customer elects to have their recurring payment set up via UPI AutoPay and selects their preferred UPI App.
2. The selected UPI app will display the mandate information including amount and frequency.
3. Once approved with their UPI PIN, the mandate will go live, allowing the merchant to automatically debit the customer’s account according to the selected schedule. Verify the active mandate status before scheduling collections.


### eNACH Mandate Setup


1. First, the merchant enables eNACH through its sponsor bank or payment provider. The arrangement uses the applicable NPCI utility code; merchants using a provider do not necessarily obtain and manage that code independently.
2. Next, when checking out, the customer will select their bank and authenticate using a supported net banking, debit card or Aadhaar flow.
3. After authentication, the mandate is verified and the NACH system assigns a Unique Mandate Reference Number (UMRN).
4. The merchant then uses this number to debit the customer’s account in accordance with the scheduled terms of the mandate. When integrating through Cashfree,[create and manage the subscription](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/create) using our supported flow and monitor its status, rather than treating a UMRN alone as confirmation that collection is ready.


##


Pre-Debit Notifications, Cancellation and Customer Controls


As part of the RBI’s e-mandate framework, issuers send consumers a pre-debit alert at least 24 hours prior to a scheduled automatic withdrawal on cards, prepaid instruments and UPI. Every e-mandate specifies how long it remains valid. The framework provides for opting out of a particular transaction or withdrawing the mandate with AFA. Separate pre-notification exceptions apply to FASTag and NCMC auto-replenishment.


Cancellation controls depend on the payment mode and applicable rules. For UPI, the RBI framework requires issuers to provide a withdrawal facility. Lending products can involve specialised mandate arrangements, so confirm the permitted cancellation workflow with your provider and lender. Our[subscription management flow](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/manage) supports cancellation and other lifecycle actions where applicable; the repayment obligation continues even if the mandate is stopped.


##


Which Recurring Payment Method Fits Your Business?


Your decision on whether to use eNACH or UPI AutoPay will depend on your target audience and the size of the recurring payment you wish to process.


**Use UPI AutoPay for consumer subscriptions:** When processing small monthly subscription payments across various consumer segments that utilize popular apps and services, including OTT and SaaS applications. These recurring payments typically fall below the limits established for UPI transactions.


**Use eNACH for high-value recurring payments:** If your business has customers who need to make recurring debits larger than those allowed in UPI transactions (i.e., loan repayments, insurance premiums, SIPs etc.), or if your business processes eligible B2B recurring payments. Check bank and account eligibility before choosing the digital route.


##


UPI AutoPay vs eNACH for EMIs, Insurance, SIPs and SaaS


**For lending and NBFCs:** eNACH can work better for big EMIs; UPI AutoPay may suit smaller repayment amounts and app-based onboarding. Our eNACH offering includes payment retries for subsequent EMIs. Collection success depends on sufficient funds, mandate validity, bank responses and the permitted retry process.


**For insurance:** The RBI’s current framework permits collection of insurance premiums via UPI AutoPay without fresh AFA up to ₹1 lakh per subsequent transaction, subject to product enablement. For higher premiums, assess eNACH or another supported flow with the required authentication. Customers do not automatically move from UPI to eNACH when a threshold is crossed.


**For mutual funds:** SIPs worth ₹1 lakh or less could be done via UPI AutoPay without fresh AFA for subsequent debits, subject to product enablement. SIPs or other mutual fund products can use eNACH with[Third-Party Validation (TPV)](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/automating-recurring-payments-with-third-party-validation-why-is-it-a-necessity-for-bfsi-sector/) to restrict mandate authorisation to the investor’s registered bank account. TPV supports account matching; it does not replace investor KYC.


**For subscriptions and SaaS:** Consumer subscriptions generally fall under the UPI limits which makes UPI AutoPay the quicker method.


##


Other Recurring Payment Methods in India


You have multiple options to make recurring payments in India besides using UPI AutoPay and eNACH. Card mandates, also known as standing instructions on cards, allow you to schedule recurring debits from a customer’s credit/debit card. The card mandates will be governed by the same RBI e-mandate framework as UPI.


A[UPI one-time mandate](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/upi-otm) is a separate collection option, not a recurring billing mandate. A one-time mandate reserves money without charging it initially. A business can then capture the entire or supported partial amount at a future date. If no capture occurs before expiry or the block is revoked, the reserved money is released back to the customer’s available balance. This model suits authorise-now, capture-later payments rather than repeated subscription renewals.


##


How We Support UPI AutoPay, eNACH and Card Mandates


Our[Subscriptions product](https://www.cashfree.com/recurring-payment/) brings UPI AutoPay, eNACH and card mandates into one place. Based on the payment method and reason for failure of debits, you can use supported retries or offer a[Payment Link](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) as a one-time recovery option. eNACH and card retries require the supported merchant action. Track collection results through[subscription webhooks](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/subscription/webhooks) and reconcile any recovery payment to the original billing cycle.


More than fifty apps are supported by UPI AutoPay through our offering. More than fifty banks are supported for eNACH, with coverage and authentication modes depending on the current bank list. Third-Party Validation provides additional functionality to eNACH as well. This feature restricts authorisation to the bank account registered for the customer, supporting your existing verification and compliance process.


##


UPI AutoPay vs eNACH: Choose by Amount, Customer and Account Eligibility


Your choice between UPI AutoPay and eNACH depends on several factors such as limits, activation speed and your customers. UPI AutoPay can be set up in seconds which suits most everyday subscriptions. eNACH supports much larger debits for eligible bank accounts. Therefore, consider offering both and let your customers choose a supported method that suits their needs. Confirm the actual amount, authentication settings and cancellation flow before going live.

FAQs


#### What are the major differences between UPI AutoPay and eNACH?


While setting up mandates via UPI app takes place in real time (as soon as users authorize), subsequent debits generally have a threshold of ₹15,000 without additional factor of authentication (AFA) for most categories; higher-value payments depend on supported AFA settings under RBI’s 2026 e-mandate framework. On the other hand, mandates authorized via supported bank authentication methods (for eNACH) may take anywhere between one day to two days to get activated through Cashfree and can handle much higher debits.


#### What is the AFA-free limit for a single transaction using UPI AutoPay?


Subsequent recurring transactions can be processed without additional factor of authentication (AFA) up to ₹15,000 per transaction while recurring transactions for insurance premiums, mutual fund subscription and credit card bill payment can be processed up to ₹1 lakh per transaction. Mandate registration and the first transaction require authentication, and the higher category threshold must be supported and enabled for your payment flow.


#### How long does it take to activate an eNACH mandate?


eNACH mandates normally get activated within one to two days through our offering, subject to bank processing and successful authorisation.


#### Can I use both UPI AutoPay and eNACH?


Yes. Businesses can utilize both for offering different services. They can opt for UPI AutoPay for small and app-based recurring transactions while opting for eNACH for high-value recurring transactions.


#### Are UPI mandates the same as eNACH mandates?


No. A UPI mandate is created and accepted in a UPI app with a UPI PIN. An eNACH mandate is authorized through the customer’s bank using a supported net banking, debit card or Aadhaar flow.


#### Is eNACH different from NACH?


Yes. eNACH is simply the digital version of NACH. It removes the requirement for the client to physically sign a paper-based NACH form and instead uses online methods of authorization.
